# A/B test: live-path replay

Experiment `triage-linear-vs-transformer-2026-08` — 3079 records from the **test** split replayed through `TriageService`, the same code path the HTTP API uses.

## Traffic split

| Version | Configured | Observed | Records |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `baseline-linear-v1` | 0.50 | 0.5076 | 1563 |
| `transformer-distilbert-v1` | 0.50 | 0.4924 | 1516 |

Chi-square goodness of fit against the configured weights: statistic 0.7174, p = 0.396985. A high p-value is the desired outcome — it means the hash-based splitter is not skewed.

## Per-version behaviour

| Version | n | Intent acc. | Category acc. | Mean conf. | Auto-route | Human review | Escalated | p50 ms | p95 ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `baseline-linear-v1` | 1563 | 0.9098 | 0.9623 | 0.8860 | 0.8618 | 0.1606 | 0.1478 | 0.5 | 0.7 |
| `transformer-distilbert-v1` | 1516 | 0.9288 | 0.9730 | 0.9586 | 0.8892 | 0.1299 | 0.1412 | 26.9 | 45.6 |

### `transformer-distilbert-v1` against control `baseline-linear-v1`

Intent accuracy 0.9098 vs 0.9288, difference **+0.0190** (95% CI -0.0002 to +0.0382), z = -1.9303, p = 0.0535658. Not significant at the 0.05 level.

This is the unpaired test. For the question "which model is better", the paired comparison in [`model_comparison.md`](model_comparison.md) is the one to use.

## Caveats

- arms see disjoint records, so this is an unpaired comparison and is less powerful than the paired McNemar test in model_comparison.md
- accuracy is only computable because this is a replay of a labelled split; live traffic carries no ground truth
- there is no business outcome metric here (handle time, reopen rate, customer satisfaction), which is what a real A/B test would decide on

## Monitoring output

Per-version insight aggregation and drift readings for this run are in [`ab_experiment.json`](ab_experiment.json) under `insights` and `drift`. Drift is near zero by construction here: the replay is drawn from the same distribution as training, so this run is a control that shows the detector does *not* fire on data it should not fire on.
